description: Probably Not(e) Bohlen-Pierce is a probabilistic quantiser for Bohlen-Pierce tuning, where a 3:1 tritave replaces the octave and holds thirteen notes, lettered C through B with H and J among them.

params.text: Sets how many notes either side of the quantised note can be chosen, 0 to 6; at 0 the quantised note is the only candidate.
An attenuverter, -100% to +100%, scaling the voltage at the input it belongs with before that voltage is added to the control's own setting.
Sets the direction of the choice: fully left only notes below the quantised note, centre both directions, fully right only notes above.
Sets the starting probability across the candidates: at 100% every candidate is equally likely, at 0% the furthest candidate falls to a tenth of the chance, rising linearly towards the centre.
Rotates the scale's note weights up or down by as many as twelve steps, which moves the weighting to a different mode of the scale.
Chooses one of ten scales: Chromatic and the nine Lambda scales.
Sets the root the scale is built on, one of the thirteen Bohlen-Pierce notes.
Shifts the quantised note by whole tritaves, -4 to +4.
Puts the note weights and the on or off state of the current scale back to the values that scale ships with.
Holds every chosen note inside the tritave of the pitch at NOTE IN when lit; unlit, chosen notes land near the incoming pitch.
Makes one volt step a whole tritave when lit, so octave-based CV drives the scale; unlit, a tritave takes 1.585V and the output tracks true Bohlen-Pierce pitch.
Switches the output between equal division of the tritave and pure whole-number ratios.
Steps through how WEIGHT SHIFT reads its input: unlit is one step of shift per volt, and the two lit states read the input as pitch, one relative to the key and one absolute.
Makes the KEY input read pitch rather than a plain sweep when lit, so the key can follow a keyboard or another quantiser; unlit, 0-10V spans the thirteen keys.
Bends the note weights from linear at 0% to logarithmic at 100%, which widens the gap between likely and unlikely notes.
Detunes the chosen note by a random amount of as much as 10 cents.
Draws the pitch randomisation from a Gaussian distribution when lit, from an even one when unlit.
Gives each polyphonic voice its own channel of the TRIGGER input when lit; unlit, every voice is clocked from the first channel.
Takes that note out of the scale or puts it back; a note that is off is never chosen.
Sets the probability weight of that note within the current scale, 0 to 100%.
Sets the chance that the note last played is barred from being chosen again; at 100% a note never repeats.

inputs.text: The pitch to be quantised; a tritave spans 1.585V unless tritave mapping is lit, and the polyphony here sets how many voices the module runs.
Voltage here is added to the setting of the control it belongs with, scaled by that control's attenuverter.
Voltage here moves through the ten scales, 0-10V spanning the whole list at a full attenuverter.
Voltage here moves the key, 0-10V spanning the thirteen keys, or reads as pitch when v/O is lit.
A trigger here switches between equal division of the tritave and pure whole-number ratios.
A trigger here chooses a new note; with nothing patched here no new note is chosen.
Takes the random number behind the note choice from this voltage, 0-10V, instead of the module's own; each polyphonic channel feeds the matching voice.
A trigger here turns tritave wrapping on or off.
Adds to the weight of that note, 0-10V covering the full range of the weight.

outputs.text: The chosen note as pitch, with the tritave shift and any pitch randomness included.
The probability weight of the note last chosen, 0-10V.
A 10V trigger each time the chosen note differs from the one before.

notes: the quantised output does not move until a trigger arrives at the trigger input; each trigger is what picks the next note.
menu: Quantize Mode — how the incoming pitch is made to fit: Closet for the nearest note, Round Lower for down, Round Upper for up. Closet is the maker's spelling of closest.
Trigger Delay — holds the trigger by five samples, for clocks that arrive before the pitch has settled.

inputs.8: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.11: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
